correctness.rationale: For fixed q, direct counting gives P(miss A), P(miss B), and P(miss both). Rewriting the covariance as a signed ratio shows R_0=1 and R_(q+1)/R_q-1 has exactly the sign of h(N-q)-ab, giving a single turn and at most one positive-to-negative crossing. Strict partial overlap ensures the ratio reaches zero while both marginal miss probabilities remain positive. Nested and disjoint cases and degeneracies are separated. The sharp five-partner example follows from ab >= (h+1)^2 >= 4h and exact fractions (1/25,1/100,-1/100,0). A standalone exact arithmetic checker enumerated 51192 uniform subsets through N=8 and 4624790 nondegenerate sign checks through N=50; these computations are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected ecology originals study attack-tolerance curves and nestedness under random species removal, not the all-parameter covariance sign across fixed quotas. Classical negative association covers disjoint neighborhoods, not overlapping hit events. No semantically equivalent one-switch theorem or sharp five-partner boundary was found in the executed published-record and literature searches. This is best-knowledge originality rather than a uniqueness certification; exact bibliographic equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: Ecological partner-loss studies commonly impose a fixed removal fraction, yet overlap of neighbors does not by itself determine whether two dependent species persist together: the covariance may switch sign, exactly once, with the partner-survival quota. The theorem supplies an explicit all-parameter criterion and a sharp smallest realizable network, while explaining why an independent-primary-loss approximation obscures the phenomenon. This offers a substantive risk-dependence characterization beyond known mean attack-tolerance curves; no general whole-community claim is made.
